subject: Pharos Health: VPC boundary diagram request + commitments
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@pharoshealth.com>, Tomás Rivera <tomas@pharoshealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pharos Health: VPC boundary diagram request + commitments

Hi Elaine / Tomás —

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the Pharos infra team and walk through your privacy constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard from you:
- All inference traffic (requests + responses) must remain within Pharos-managed VPC peering or private link; no customer PII should traverse public internet egress from the Redwood side.
- Minimal logs needed for debugging; if retained, query logs must be pseudonymized and stored for no more than 90 days.
- Primary model serving to run in your AWS us-west-2 account (Private deployment).

Redwood commitments and asks:
1) We will produce a VPC boundary diagram showing inbound/outbound flows, NAT/Egress points, and required security groups. (Action: Redwood SE will draft and share.)
2) We need a short list of Pharos IP ranges that we can allow-list for the peering endpoints.
3) Confirm whether S3 artifacts (model checkpoints) are acceptable in your account or must be held on-prem.
4) We’ll share SOC 2 summary and an evidence template; Pharos can fill gaps for procurement.

Next steps / owners: 
- Lauren (SE) to send a first-pass boundary diagram and egress controls doc by EOD Mon.
- Elaine/Tomás to confirm IP ranges + retention ceiling for debug logs (if different from 90 days).
- Marcus to propose a mutual action plan and updated quote once deployment scope (airgap vs private link) is confirmed.

Attachments: I’ll include a short SOC2 summary and a template for evidence requests.

Thanks — will follow up with Lauren’s diagram shortly.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pharos Health: VPC boundary diagram request + commitments

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming we need zero public egress for PII payloads; inference responses can be returned over the private link only.
- For debug logs: 30 days preferred, 90 days acceptable with explicit pseudonymization (hashing user ids + salt managed by Pharos).
- IP ranges: I can pull the current NAT IPs and send by EOD Tue. We also need to know whether Redwood will maintain any outbound connections for telemetry or automatic model updates — that would need explicit approval.

Questions: 
1) If we choose an air-gapped/on-prem option later, what components would require on-prem placement vs what can remain controlled by Redwood’s control plane?
2) Can you confirm whether KV cache warmers would ever initiate external connections (we need that to remain inside our network).

We’re running this through procurement in parallel; they’ll expect the SOC2 summary and an evidence template.

Elaine Park
Director, IT Security | Pharos Health
elaine@pharoshealth.com

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the clarifications. I’ve sketched a first-pass VPC boundary diagram and included notes on egress controls and components that require connectivity. High-level answers to your questions below; diagram attached.

Answers / notes:
- Telemetry/Control Plane: For the Private deployment we propose a customer-hosted data plane (in your account) with a small control-plane agent that speaks to Redwood control plane over an authenticated TLS connection on outbound port 443. If you require fully air-gapped, the control-plane agent can be replaced with an offline deploy — that adds a weekly manual artifact sync process.
- KV cache warmers and model artifacts will run in the customer VPC (no external egress). Automatic model updates are optional; if enabled, updates fetch artifacts from a signed, allow-listed endpoint — we can instead provide offline artifact bundles for air-gapped installs.
- Logging: we can configure the runtime to redact user identifiers before writing traces; by default debug traces are not shipped to Redwood unless explicitly enabled.

Attachments included: redwood_vpc_boundary_sketch.png (diagram), and a short notes doc. I marked the items that require procurement sign-off.

Action items I’ll take: 
- Finalize diagram + call out exact security groups and subnet mapping by Tue EOD.
- Expand the egress control table to show port/IP requirements for the optional control-plane traffic.

If anything in the diagram looks off, flag it and I’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

Vivek —

Forwarding the thread from Pharos. Elaine pushed back on external egress and asked for an air-gapped option explanation and confirmation that KV cache warmers won’t reach out of the customer VPC. Lauren’s diagram (attached) answers most of this, but procurement will want an explicit statement on audit/log retention settings. 

Two asks for you: 
1) Approve a one-time exception to allow a signed, allow-listed update endpoint (if Pharos chooses auto-updates) OR confirm we present the offline artifact workflow as the default for them. Offline workflow adds operational effort but is acceptable to Pharos.
2) Approve offering a 90-day max retention with pseudonymization, or push back to 30 days as a discount/reduced-fee concession? Procurement may ask for that concession in contract negotiations.

If you’re OK, I’ll reply to Elaine with the approved options and an updated mutual action plan.

—Marcus

Thanks everyone — diagram looks good and captures the flow we expected. A couple final points before procurement moves to the SOW: 

- Please include an explicit clause that model artifact pushes are only performed via signed artifact bundles and that those bundles can be provided offline (no outbound fetch) for the first 12 months if required.
- We’ll provide the NAT IP ranges by end of day.
- For log retention, we can accept the 90-day retention if Redwood includes pseudonymization and an SLA clause that allows us to request immediate deletion of specific traces on-demand. Please include the deletion API in the security appendix.

If you can update the action plan with those specifics I’ll route it to procurement. After procurement OKs, we’ll schedule an install readiness call.

Regards,
